sources.entry: ToolJet - Low-code framework to build & deploy internal tools with minimal engineering effort (alternative to Retool and Mendix). (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker/K8S
ToolJet | Low-code platform for internal tools and business apps

summary.one_liner: ToolJet is an open-source low-code platform for building and deploying internal tools such as admin panels, dashboards, and operational apps on top of existing databases, APIs, and SaaS systems.
summary.what_it_does: ToolJet provides a visual app builder with 80+ responsive components (tables, charts, forms, lists) and multi-page apps with multiplayer editing. It connects to 90+ data sources including databases, APIs, cloud storage, and SaaS tools. It includes a built-in no-code database called ToolJet Database and supports running JavaScript and Python inside apps. The Community Edition is self-hostable with Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, Azure, and other options. The README also describes an Enterprise tier with AI app generation, workflows, modules, RBAC, SCIM, GitSync, and multi-environment management, plus an MCP server so coding agents can build ToolJet apps.
use_cases: create operational dashboards on existing databases
connect a team's APIs and SaaS tools to one app
automate multi-step workflows on a schedule or webhook
how_to_run: docker run --name tooljet --restart unless-stopped -p 80:80 --platform linux/amd64 -v tooljet_data:/var/lib/postgresql/13/main tooljet/try:ee-lts-latest
Alternatively, sign up for ToolJet Cloud (hosted).
For production self-hosting, follow the deployment guides for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS, GCP, Azure, or OpenShift.
notable: Built-in MCP server lets coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients build and edit apps
Covers 90+ data sources and 80+ UI components in the visual builder
Community Edition is self-hostable with multiple deployment guides
Uses git-flow branching with develop as base branch and LTS tags for stability
Available on AWS and Azure Marketplaces
caveats: Many advanced features (AI, workflows, modules, SCIM, GitSync, white-labeling, SLAs) are Enterprise-only
ToolJet MCP is currently in beta
The Docker quick-start image is intended for trying it out; the README points to deployment docs for production
